title: An alias inside the node that redefines its anchor is a cycle
notes: An alias refers to the most recent preceding node with its name (section 7.1). In `c: &b [ *b ]` that is the sequence being defined, not the earlier `&b 1` on the line above, so the sequence contains itself. A graph with a cycle is allowed by the data model, but a value in the kit's JSON-comparable form cannot hold one, so a value load must refuse it. The category is not fixed, because libraries call this a syntax, limit or recursion error. What it must never do is read the alias as the earlier `1` and answer `{a: 1, c: [1]}`. The kit states this as a convention of its value form, not as a rule of the specification, and the event stream is not checked, because a library may stream the events of a valid document.

provenance.reference: Found while reading the source of a library whose alias lookup used the earlier anchor of the same name and so loaded the input as a finite value.
